rules.sentence: Participants will gain an understanding of ulnar neuropathy's clinical manifestations, including paresthesias of the fourth and fifth digits, hand weakness, impaired grip and pinch strength, and, in advanced disease, intrinsic muscle atrophy, as well as the diagnostic processes that rely on a focused clinical evaluation supported by electrodiagnostic studies and imaging when structural causes are suspected, the management strategies, and the complications including persistent sensory loss, motor deficits, or progressive deformity.
Prevention of compression, along with early diagnosis and treatment, is essential for optimizing prognosis, as treatment outcomes are often disappointing once axonal damage has developed.
